claims.text: A Kubernetes cluster consists of a control plane plus a set of worker machines called nodes that run containerized applications; the control plane manages the nodes and stores cluster state.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Overview > Cluster Architecture; Kubernetes Components

claims.text: The control plane makes global decisions about the cluster, such as scheduling (choosing which node runs what), and keeps the record of the cluster's state.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Overview > Components (Control Plane Components)

claims.text: In the donhang kind cluster the control-plane node carries the taint node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule, so application containers are not placed on it; the two workers have no taint.
claims.source_hint: executed: kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,TAINTS:.spec.taints; kubernetes.io well-known taints

claims.text: Adding a worker node adds capacity for more containers; the control plane's role is unchanged, it gains one more node to choose from.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Architecture > Nodes (adding nodes, self-registration)

claims.text: kind runs local Kubernetes clusters using Docker container 'nodes'; each node is a container from the kindest/node image running the Kubernetes node software inside.
claims.source_hint: kind.sigs.k8s.io: home page and Quick Start (node images); executed docker ps

claims.text: Containers Kubernetes starts on a kind node run inside that node container (its own runtime, containerd), so docker ps on the host shows the node containers but none of the containers inside them.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Design / Initial design (containerd inside node); executed: docker ps shows 3 kindest/node containers while donhang Pods run

claims.text: deploy/k8s/kind-config.yaml@stage-2 (lines 6-14): kind Cluster, apiVersion kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4, one control-plane node and two worker nodes, each image kindest/node:v1.34.11@sha256:44e222ee...

In name:tag@sha256:digest the tag names the version (kindest/node v1.34.11 = Kubernetes v1.34.11) and the digest pins the exact image content; kind-config.yaml lines 1-2 of config: kind: Cluster, apiVersion kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Configuration > nodes image; kind release v0.33.0 notes (image list with digests); Docker docs image digest

claims.text: cluster-up.sh@stage-2: if donhang exists, prints 'The cluster donhang already exists.' and runs kubectl config use-context kind-donhang; else kind create cluster --name donhang --config ... --wait 180s piped to awk that cuts the final greeting; then kubectl wait.

kind create cluster --wait 180s waits up to 180 seconds for the control-plane node to be ready before returning; kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready nodes --all --timeout=180s waits up to 180 s for every node.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Quick Start (--wait); kind create cluster --help

claims.text: kind create cluster output (outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/cluster-up.txt) shows Starting control-plane before Joining worker nodes, and ends with Set kubectl context to "kind-donhang".
The scripts/k8s scripts run on the host, beside Docker, not inside the lab box, because kind needs Docker to start node containers (lab box has no Docker access).
docker ps --format "{{.Names}}  {{.Image}}" | grep kindest prints donhang-control-plane, donhang-worker, donhang-worker2, each with image kindest/node:v1.34.11.
claims.source_hint: executed on author's machine with the donhang kind cluster running (Docker 28.0.1)

claims.text: In a production cluster each node is a separate physical or virtual machine.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Architecture > Nodes ('A node may be a virtual or physical machine')

claims.text: Each kind node is a Docker container; by default a container has no resource constraints and shares the host's CPU and memory, so all nodes share one laptop's CPU and memory.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: Engine > Containers > Resource constraints

claims.text: The lab box (lab/Dockerfile@stage-2: openssh-server + openssl, git, psql, procps, redis) has no Docker installed and no Docker socket mounted (docker-compose.yml lab volumes), so kind cannot run there.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2 lab/Dockerfile; docker-compose.yml lab service volumes; STAGE.md Prerequisites

claims.text: The first kind create cluster downloads the kindest/node image ('Ensuring node image' step) and can take several minutes; later runs of cluster-up.sh with the cluster present return at once.
